perspective:
From Angela’s available perspective:

- She and Kevin have been close friends since high school. She knows Kevin works in construction and has noticed he seems unhappy with his job.
- At the coffee meeting she initiated, Kevin told her work was “the usual grind,” that he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions. She suggested a different job or career path. Kevin said he had thought about it but felt overwhelmed and unsure where to start. She offered to figure out options together. Kevin thanked her and said her support mattered.
- Angela found job openings and a career counseling service and shared them with Kevin. He thanked her, said she “went all out,” and told her he had been thinking a lot and was interested in something creative, possibly design or architecture. She encouraged him and suggested he check the resources. He said he would.
- Angela believed Kevin was hesitant about changing careers. Feeling frustrated and worried, she arranged a meeting with a career coach and told Kevin. He said she didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. She encouraged him to try it; he agreed to give it a shot. She promised to support him.
- Angela later checked in about the career coach. Kevin told her the coach was helpful, that he had started online design courses, and that he felt more confident. She said she was proud and asked if she could help further. He said just knowing she was there was enough.
- By the final scenario, Angela believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career. She organized a small celebration party and told him he deserved it. Kevin thanked her, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without her. She said he did the hard work and invited him to enjoy the party.
- Angela’s own relevant feelings and actions include: concern, support, hope, frustration/worry about Kevin’s hesitation, pride/relief, and happiness/satisfaction. She invited Kevin to coffee, researched resources, arranged the career coach meeting, checked in, and organized the celebration.

She has no access to hidden events or Kevin’s private thoughts beyond what he expressed to her, nor to narrator-only information.
